name: agent-step-toolkit
description: Build agent-step LangGraph agents — a ReAct agent fronted by one batching tool over a deterministic flow-controller runner (vendored and versioned; agent-step 4.1.0). Bootstrap a project (runner library + streaming CLI + graph/state/prompt scaffold + the required local sandbox service), then add domain tools declaratively: each action declares its params by field KIND (caller digits, caller text, a judged enum or flag, a relayed value), its prereqs and its verdict ROWS — summary, doctrine, state write, effects, the standing ask the outcome leaves behind, one authority per outcome — and its executor just names the verdict. Every sentence has one owner: the engine owns the machinery and its model-facing language — composed action descriptions, per-gate and standing-ask reply contracts, the spliceable turn-protocol prompt fragment, and instruction text the model follows and never speaks — while everything a caller can hear (row summaries, read-backs, ask text, handoff closings) is rendered by the host from state. Mechanisms are configuration, not prompt prose — confirmation propose/execute gates with attempt budgets and stored-byte repetition, OTP and double-entry match gates, multi-turn flows, paginated reads, state-satisfied inputs (an action satisfied from values already in state, silently or with the caller's consent), one config-level invalidation table, universal bounded patience (the engine counts unusable captures and refusals and escalates into the configured handoff by itself; its numbers are deployment-level AGENT_STEP_* tolerances), typed refusal kinds with a misuse limit, an engine-enforced abort policy, verdict rows that declare what happens next independently of success, optional required tool calling (every model turn is a tool call: speech through a library control with engine-inserted fixed text, misuse classified on every call, each result bounding the next call), typed handoff routes, and a state-resolved handback envelope with orchestrator/specialized agent roles plus off-topic delegation, and a handback observer for side effects that must follow the outcome. Graph state is one Zod schema (reducers + invoke-boundary validation, channel-completeness enforced at construction). Also: flow documentation for any agent-step agent (from a prose description, an existing codebase, or specs and a walkthrough — one validated spec generating a Markdown design, an auto-laid-out interactive step graph and an xlsx step sheet, with a verification script), the twelve measured host-architecture design principles, porting an existing project onto agent-step, Kafka run-tracing observability via the companion kafka-observability plugin, the three-layer test methodology (runner unit / sandbox / prompt-input), and a channel-middleware contract audit.
